opportunities.title: Henry Moore Grants

amount.raw: Maximum grant £20,000 (New Projects and Commissions, Acquisitions and Collections, Long-Term Research); £5,000 (Conferences, Lectures and Publications); £2,500 (Research and Travel)

opportunities.eligibility_summary: UK and international non-profit organisations (must have been operating as non-profit for at least 12 months) for New Projects and Commissions, Acquisitions and Collections, Conferences/Lectures/Publications, and Long-Term Research categories. Individual sculpture historians, academics and conservators for the Research and Travel category. Not open to individuals developing their own artistic practice.
opportunities.summary: Grants supporting the growth and development of sculpture across historical, modern and contemporary registers, and research expanding the appreciation of sculpture. Categories: New Projects and Commissions (exhibitions, catalogues, commissions); Acquisitions and Collections; Conferences, Lectures and Publications; Long-Term Research; and Research and Travel grants for individuals. Applications considered four times per year; the Autumn round is currently open.

opportunities.title: Visiting Research Fellowships

amount.raw: Expenses allocation: UK up to £600, Europe up to £700, Rest of world up to £1,000, plus accommodation in Leeds or Hertfordshire

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Academics, curators, artists and established scholars working on historic and contemporary sculpture. Fellowships at Studios & Gardens are restricted to projects related to Henry Moore. Artist Research Fellowships are for research only (no studio facilities).
opportunities.summary: Fellowships enabling artists and researchers to spend a month using the Henry Moore Institute's research facilities in Leeds or Hertfordshire, including accommodation, travel and subsistence. Types: Visiting Research Fellowships, Artist Research Fellowships, and Senior Fellowships (six weeks). Applications are currently closed for 2026/27; the next round opens in spring 2027.

opportunities.title: Dissertation Prize

amount.raw: £250 cash prize for BA dissertation and £250 cash prize for MA dissertation, plus £50 of Henry Moore Institute publications

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Open to BA and MA students of all disciplines at UK universities, for a dissertation submitted within the past academic year. Dissertation must relate directly to sculpture and not have been previously published.
opportunities.summary: Two annual prizes for outstanding extended writing on contemporary, modern or historical sculpture, awarded to BA and MA students. Submissions for the 2026 prize will open in autumn.
